owner_question: Keep current old/custom-wired short clip or try new longer factory-wired clip?
recommendation: Try one new40cm clip next on same C8375-A/FDO2742M0FK/U1, retaining Pi/linux_spi0.0/requested100kHz and active1.8V adapter. Preserve current short/custom assembly and its verified baseline.
rationale: Current clip already produced independently verified repeatable bounded reads; those still differ systematically from references. A different clip/contact/cable assembly offers independent read-path evidence. Further unchanged reads alone add little.
tradeoff: Factory assembly may reduce custom-contact variability; greater cable length may reduce electrical margin. Neither advantage nor improvement is established. Entire assembly changes, so any result cannot isolate length versus contact construction.
physical_plan: Shut down Pi and unplug supply before touching wires/clip; keep CH341A removed and router power/other cables/CR2032 isolated.
Label first new40cm clip New40cm-A, leaving second unused; current short clip remains separate and intact.

Inspect new clip/breakout while detached; verify pin1 orientation, wide SOIC16 fit and eight actual output-to-package connections. Factory assembly is not a pin-map guarantee. Do not infer mappings from ribbon color or force generic DIP8 hookup.
Retain Pi input harness/active1.8V adapter and requested100kHz; change only the clip/cable assembly on same physical U1.
Reconfirm chassis/U1/current isolation and exclusive programmer ownership, then verify loaded P1 supply1.7-2.0V.
ID first, then two independent reads of same two64KiB regions if ID and voltage acceptable; compare each new pair and against current-short baseline and references.

Stop on failed ID/voltage or unreliable pair; preserve failures. If different bytes appear, investigate changed path without treating either read as automatically correct. If same bytes appear, remaining bank/content/systematic errors still require analysis.
